title: IT stocks surge 3.6% as Nifty edges up; rupee slips to 92.44 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Information technology shares led the market on Thursday, with the Nifty IT index gaining 3.66 per cent and rising nearly 8 per cent over the past week, as investors rotated out of global AI-linked stocks.

Realty, capital markets and metal stocks also advanced, offsetting declines in FMCG, auto and banks on the Sensex’s monthly expiry day.

The Nifty 50 closed at 25,884.50, up 65.25 points or 0.25 per cent, after touching an intraday high of 25,974.95 and a low of 25,733.50. The Sensex ended at 84,328.59, up 390.31 points or 0.46 per cent. Bank Nifty fell 167.95 points, or 0.26 per cent, to 63,535.30.

Among Nifty constituents, HCL Technologies gained 6.42 per cent, BSE 5.70 per cent, TCS 4.89 per cent and Infosys 4.69 per cent, according to SBI Securities.

Asian Paints fell 2.98 per cent, Bajaj Finance 2.96 per cent, Shriram Finance 2.84 per cent and Nestle India 2.81 per cent.

Nifty Realty rose 3.27 per cent and Nifty Metal 1.17 per cent, while Nifty FMCG fell 0.94 per cent and Nifty Auto 0.69 per cent. MCX shares rose 8 per cent to a record high on the recovery in gold and silver. Sugar stocks rose up to 14 per cent after the sugar industry body projected 2026-27 output at 26.5 million tonnes, down from 27.9 million tonnes.

Sectoral performance showed strong buying interest in technology and real estate counters. According to Mayank Jain, Market Analyst at PhonePe Invest, “Conversely, mild selling pressure weighed on Nifty FMCG, Nifty Auto, Nifty PSU Bank, Bank Nifty and Nifty Financial Services.

The Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.32 per cent and the Smallcap 100 rose 0.74 per cent. Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, said FMCG lagged “after the Supreme Court’s call for separate warning labels raised compliance concerns for the sector.”

Foreign portfolio investors have put a record $15.16 billion into Indian equities this month.

The rupee closed at 92.44 against the dollar, down 20 paise, after touching an eight-month high on Wednesday.

HDFC Securities’ Dilip Parmar said traders are watching for a possible central bank swap amid strong November dollar inflows, which could limit further gains.

Brent crude traded near $94 to $95 a barrel after reports of an attack on a Saudi refinery. Gold and silver rebounded in domestic trade.

The US has proposed 25 per cent tariffs on India, falling to 17 per cent if a bilateral trade deal is finalised. Sarvam Goel, Founder of Pocketful said nothing can take effect before January, adding that “the G20 meeting in mid-December” is the date to watch for the trade deal.

“Near-term sentiment remains constructive but volatile,” Nair said, adding that foreign liquidity should help limit the downside while global rates, crude and trade talks could cap valuations.

Next week brings India’s second-quarter GDP data on Monday, followed by the RBI’s policy decision on December 4. The US Federal Reserve meets on December 8–9, where a 25-basis-point hike is expected. Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking said a close above 26,000 is needed for the Nifty to move toward its record high of 26,373.
